ⓘ How to read these numbers

Raw Detections = every window where the FCA lattice similarity dropped enough to trigger an alarm. One real drift event typically causes several consecutive alarms (the stream needs a few windows to stabilise after the change).

Merged Episodes = alarms that are within merge_gap = 100 instances of each other are collapsed into a single episode. This gives the true count of distinct concept-drift events in the stream.

Drift type is classified per episode using Z-score analysis of ΔLt relative to the local signal baseline: Sudden (≥2.5σ spike) • Gradual (sustained moderate elevation) • Incremental (slow monotonic build-up) • Recurring (similarity to past stable state ≥ threshold).

Analysis Graphs

Lattice Change (ΔL) — Advanced View

Primary drift signal with adaptive threshold (orange line). Shows changes in the formal concept lattice between consecutive sliding windows, with Moving Average smoothing (dark blue line) for noise reduction. Merged drift episodes are color-coded by type. The gray hatched zone marks the warm-up period excluded from analysis. The adaptive threshold μ±Nσ dynamically adjusts sensitivity based on recent signal variance.

Lattice Similarity — Trend

Similarity comparison between consecutive concept lattices with mean ±σ band (green fill). Lower similarity = greater structural drift. Moving Average smoothing reduces oscillations for clear trend identification. Red X markers indicate detected drift points. Y-axis bounded [0,1] for normalized interpretation.

Drift Type Distribution — Analysis

Comprehensive distribution analysis with pie chart, histogram + KDE curve, stacked bar chart by stream regions, and a statistics panel. Shows total drift count, drift density, spatial distribution, and type breakdown. Identifies which types of concept changes occur most frequently in the data stream and how they evolve over time.

Synchronized View — ΔL + Similarity

Dual-axis visualization combining ΔL (lower panel, red) and Similarity (upper panel, blue) on a shared x-axis. Enables direct visual comparison of both metrics and detection of temporal correlations. Each metric uses its own y-axis scale for optimal readability. Provides a holistic view of drift dynamics.
